summary_paragraph: A man with a history of cocaine-induced cardiomyopathy, systolic heart failure, COPD, and chronic kidney disease was admitted for right-sided pleuritic chest pain. Initial concern for pulmonary embolism was ruled out with a negative D-dimer and VQ scan, and lower extremity ultrasound showed no DVT. The chest pain was determined to be musculoskeletal, likely from coughing, and resolved during the admission. He was found to be fluid-overloaded, with weight above his dry weight and mild pulmonary edema, prompting IV diuresis. He was transitioned back to home torsemide with the addition of weekly metolazone. Losartan was reduced to 12.5 mg daily due to kidney concerns. His troponin elevation was attributed to chronic heart and kidney disease. He remained stable, with improved volume status and resolution of symptoms, and was discharged home with follow-up for a lung nodule and iron deficiency anemia.
problems: Acute on chronic systolic heart failure
Diabetes with other specified manifestations, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
Personal history of venous thrombosis and embolism
